title: Timeline of a project or research journey: how did the work evolve?
summary: A horizontal time line with dated events alternately above and below, coloured by the kind of event. It shows the order of steps, setbacks and outcomes, and invites a check on whether the spacing is proportional to time.

media.alt: Horizontal timeline with seven dated events alternating above and below the line, coloured by type, from January 2024 to June 2025.
media.caption: Reference render with synthetic demonstration data (design-system gallery).

source.note: Plot class from the design system's plot taxonomy; synthetic demonstration data.

read_the_figure.question: How did the work evolve?
read_the_figure.axes: One horizontal axis: time, flowing left to right with an arrow. Seven events from Jan 2024 to Jun 2025, each a dot with a stem and a dated box, alternating above and below. Colour: teal main line, sky validation, rose setback, amber outcome (stated in the footer).
look_at: What is the order of events, and what are the dates?
Which events are setbacks and which are validations (colour)?
Are the intervals between dots equal when the dates say they are not?
What is the first and the last event, and what is the total span?
read_the_figure.proves: It documents the sequence and the claimed dates. It does not show effort, duration of each phase, or why a setback happened.
if_wrong: Spacing not proportional to time: a 2 month gap drawn as long as a 3 month gap misleads.
Missing dates: an order without dates cannot be checked.
Colours without a key: the reader cannot tell a setback from an outcome.

terms.meaning: A line representing time with events placed on it in order.
A dated event that marks a result or a decision.
An axis on which distance is proportional to elapsed time.
Equal gaps between events whatever the real time between them.
An event that shows a problem or a failed attempt; as informative as a success.

remember: Position is time; direction is the arrow.
Dates must be on every event.
Equal gaps mean 'proportional' only if the dates are equally spaced.
Colour carries event type; read the footer.

understand.title: Marks and encodings
understand.text: Position along the line encodes time. A coloured dot with a stem links the instant to a box above or below, alternating so labels do not collide. The box holds the date in bold and a short description. Colour encodes the type of event (teal main line, sky validation, rose setback, amber outcome); the footer is the key. The arrow shows direction.

understand.title: Why this form answers the question
understand.text: A journey is a sequence with a few turning points. A line with labelled dots shows order immediately, and alternating the labels keeps the text short and readable. Colour of the type lets the reader see the shape of the story at a glance: where the validations cluster, where the setback fell.

understand.title: Read this reference render
understand.text: Q1: What is the sequence? Problem framed (Jan 2024), baseline model (Mar 2024), first failure mode (Jun 2024), new method idea (Sep 2024), validated on rig (Dec 2024), scale-up (Mar 2025), write-up (Jun 2025). Q2: Which are the setbacks and the outcomes? Only one rose box: first failure mode (Jun 2024); one amber: write-up (Jun 2025); two sky for validation: baseline model and validation on the rig. Q3: Is the spacing proportional? No. The dates give gaps of 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3 months over a 17 month span, but the drawn gaps are almost all the same (about 1.6 to 1.7 units).

understand.title: The must-check list, explained
understand.text: Dates: each box carries month and year, which lets the reader check order and spacing. A timeline with only phrases is a list; with dates it can be audited.

understand.title: How it misleads
understand.text: Spacing can mislead. Here the dots are about 1.6 to 1.7 units apart each, while the real gaps are 2 months (Jan to Mar 2024) and 3 months for all the others. If the axis were proportional to days the first gap would be 1.15 units rather than 1.6, 39 percent shorter. The timeline selects events: a long quiet period is invisible, and the dots suggest equal importance. It shows what happened, not why.

understand.title: Alternatives
understand.text: A Gantt chart shows durations and overlaps. A table of date, event, outcome, evidence is exact. A progress curve of a metric over time shows effect. A swimlane timeline separates parallel strands.

understand.title: A variant to create
understand.text: Make the axis proportional with month ticks, draw phases as bars between milestones and add a metric curve below showing the model error over time.

steps.title: Proportional placement on the axis
steps.note: With t in days: Jan 2024 = 0, Mar 2024 = 60, ..., Jun 2025 = 517 days; W = 9.9 units gives the Mar 2024 dot at 1.65 on this scale (drawn at 2.1).

steps.title: Gap between events
steps.note: Compare the ratios of drawn gaps to the ratios of true gaps.

worked.title: Where should the dots be on a proportional axis?
worked.problem: Events on 1 Jan 2024, 1 Mar 2024 and 1 Jun 2025 (the last is the write-up). The axis runs 9.9 units from the first to the last event. Place the middle event.

solution.text: Day numbers (2024 is a leap year).

worked.answer: 1.65 units from the left of the frame (0.5 + 1.15): the render puts it at 2.1, so the drawn spacing is not proportional.

analyze.q: A reader says the project 'sped up after the setback'. What on this chart could support or refute that?
What does the alternating layout hide or help?

evaluate.q: Is a timeline a good way to show that the method works?
evaluate.hint: What evidence does it not show?

create: Redraw with a proportional axis and mark phases as bars.
Add a row of evidence links (report, dataset) for each event.

checks.q: Why does every event need a date?
checks.answer: So that order and gaps can be checked.

checks.q: Events at day 0, 60 and 517. Fraction of the span at the second event?
The picture shows six equal gaps. The dates show 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3 months. What impression is created?
checks.answer: The first phase looks as long as the others, so the early work seems slower than it was.
